beginner.headline: Trump and Xi Meet: Warm Words, Little Progress on Key Issues
beginner.brief: US President Donald Trump and China's President Xi Jinping met for a big dinner. They exchanged warm words at the dinner, but they did not show much progress on big issues. Many business leaders and tech company heads also went to the dinner. President Trump gave President Xi a sculpture of a bald eagle as a gift. The dinner food had American and Chinese styles. They will meet again for tea the next day.

intermediate.headline: Trump and Xi Meet: Warm Words, Little Progress on Key Issues
intermediate.brief: US and China's presidents shared polite words at a White House state dinner, but showed little sign of progress on important issues. Xi mentioned they had "in-depth exchanges" and "common understanding" on many topics, yet crucial matters dividing the two powerful countries were barely discussed. China thinks the U.S. wants to limit its growth as a superpower, especially regarding trade, technology, and Taiwan. Trump hoped to make deals on trade and tariffs, such as reducing Chinese taxes on American goods. However, tensions remained, especially concerning Taiwan, which Beijing claims as its own. The U.S. is legally required to help Taiwan defend itself, but Trump delayed a large arms package after Xi's warning. Trump was open about his goals for artificial intelligence (AI) and saw China as the main competitor in its development. Despite Xi's comment on AI needing "human control," there was little sign of any real progress on this topic during their talks. As a gesture, Trump gave the Chinese president a sculpture of a bald eagle, America's national symbol. Guests at the dinner ate from tables with red tablecloths, a color symbolizing luck and good fortune in China.

advanced.headline: US and China Exchange Warm Words Amid Lingering Tensions
advanced.brief: US President Donald Trump and China's President Xi Jinping exchanged warm words at a lavish White House state dinner but gave little indication of progress on pressing issues. Despite diplomatic niceties and gifts, little was shared on substantial issues separating the leaders. Xi stressed that they should ensure AI remain "under human control" and act "as responsible major countries". Trump toasted a future of "harmony, peace and success" for both nations. But tensions remain despite the diplomatic niceties, including over Taiwan, which Beijing claims. Xi urged Trump earlier in the day to take the "correct position" on the self-governing island amid a weapons package paused by Trump. China believes the US is trying to contain its rise as a superpower, and it wants Washington to stay out of its way. Trump has meanwhile been expected to aim for deals around trade and tariffs during the visit, like lowering Chinese tariffs on American goods. Billionaire business leaders and US tech CEOs joined the leaders at the extravagant dinner late on Thursday. The US is legally bound to provide Taiwan with the means to defend itself, but Trump delayed approving a $14bn arms package for it. OpenAI's Sam Altman, Google's Sundar Pichai, and Amazon's Jeff Bezos were also present, as were Mark Zuckerberg and Jeff Yass, the American billionaire who owns a share of TikTok. The evening instead marked a continuation of the lavish welcome Xi has so far received in the US.
